expected: El fareeⱯ saggel talata bonṭ el naharda.
tests_for: 'point' → bonṭ — here staying SINGULAR after 'talata' (three) rather than taking the plural bonṭat, unlike the regular Arabic 3-10-takes-plural pattern. Confirms this is a memorized per-word/per-construction fact, not a rule to derive.
ث (ثعلب, 'fox') merges to t in colloquial (not s), plus a memorized word-final gemination (taⲴlabb, not taⲴlab) — this word can't be handled by a single 'ث merges to X' rule.

ثلاثة ('three') merges ث→t here too (talat), matching tha-01's direction — but note it's the elided 'talat' form (before a counted noun), NOT the standalone 'talata' seen with 'talata bonṭ' elsewhere in this set. That contrast is itself worth testing: the model shouldn't apply one fixed form of 'three' everywhere.

الليلة ('the night') must resolve to 'el lééla', not 'el layla' — same Latin letters as the name Layla would produce if the model defaults to the more common Franco spelling instead of recognizing which word is meant.

Direct contrast with homo-01 — here 'Layla' IS correct, since it's the proper name (ليلى) in the novel title, not the common noun 'night'. A model that always writes 'lééla' regardless of context fails this one; a model that always writes 'layla' fails homo-01. Both must be handled correctly by the same model to show real disambiguation, not a coin flip.
